No held evidence that the conversion permission was exercised (employees recommended/converted) or that a later instrument ended it. Acquisition: Comptroller General/Civil Service Commission records of conversions under EO 8457, or a later order superseding it; then a TERM:/ACT: record.
notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: I re-hashed (sha d864f090...) and read the whole held text, which is the Appropriation-style mirror transcription (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false). EO 8457 (signed 1940-06-17) permits GAO employees appointed before 1 July 1935 without regard to civil-service law, whose continuance until 30 June 1940 was authorized by EO 8137, to be further continued and to acquire competitive classified status on the Comptroller General's recommendation, subject to four provisos, and it classifies the affected positions from 'this date'. Its best reading is a one-time conversion permission that would be exhausted by performance, and the classification of positions is a surviving consequence rather than a command. But nothing held shows the permission was used, when, or that anything ended it. The four TERM: records are machine leads: the 'until_event' date 1935-07-01 is only the appointment cut-off, and the 'report_deadline' kind is a mislabel, so none shows an end. Cruden finds no held order citing EO 8457. Under the 2026-10-28 ruling, 'known within an interval' differs from 'not established whether it occurred', and here performance is not established, so I recommend neither NO nor YES. The text is also a transcription, so approval is withheld.
